texts.preamble: Shiv Narayan vs State Of U.P. And Another on 24 May, 2024 Author: Samit Gopal Bench: Samit Gopal High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:94946 Court No. - 87 Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 4079 of 2017 Revisionist :- Shiv Narayan Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Revisionist :- Bharat Singh Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A. Hon'ble Samit Gopal,J. 1.
texts.facts: The brief facts of the case are that Suresh Chandra Sharma, the Food Inspector found the revisionist carrying milk for sale which was told to him to be mixed milk of buffalo and cow on 27.05.1996 at 08:00 AM, on which he was stopped and asked for a license, which could not be produced by the revisionist. On a suspicion of the milk being adulterated, he purchased 750 mili gram of milk and prepared its receipt and gave money to the accused. He then prepared the other documents and prepared three bottles of the milk in equal quantities and one of the bottles was sent to the public analyst for examination. The public analyst vide his report dated 09.07.1996 opined that the mixed milk was deficient by 91% of milk fat and milk solids not fat by about 13%. The sanction was obtained by C.M.O. concerned and a complaint dated 07.01.1997 was filed. Subsequent to filing of the complaint, notice under Section 13(2) of the Act is said to have been sent to the accused on 13.01.1997. The court of Judicial Magistrate (Economic Offences), Chandausi vide order dated 19.07.2006 framed charges against the accused under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 to which, the accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 5. The trial started, in which the complainant Suresh Chandra Sharma was examined as P.W.-1, Anil Verma, the Food Clerk in the Office of the C.M.O. concerned was examined as P.W.-2. The accused in his statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. denied the prosecution case. The revision was admitted on the said date. 6. From the said fact, it is clear that the appellant remained in jail for about four months and fifteen days during trial, appeal and till the time of being granted bail. Subsequently, since there was no representation on behalf of the revisionist in the present revision, non bailable warrant was issued against him and he was directed to be arrested and lodged in jail vide order dated 01.11.2023. In compliance of the same, the revisionist was arrested on 16.11.2023 and was lodged in jail and then was directed to be released on bail vide order dated 15.03.2024 and thus, he remained in jail for about 3 months and 29 days.
texts.arguments: Shiv Narayan vs State Of U.P. And Another on 24 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54735291/ 2 7. Learned counsel for the revisionist submits that the incident in the present case is of 27.05.1996 and as such, 28 years have passed. He further submitted that the revisionist in his statement recorded under Section 313 Cr.P.C. on 04.07.2012 disclosed his age as 42 years, which was not disputed and there was no contrary finding of the concerned trial court with regards the same as per the General Rules (Criminal) and as such, now he would be about 54 years of age. He further submitted that in so far as the material collected and tested is concerned, although the same was found to be deficient for milk fat and milk solids not fat but there was nothing reported in the same to make it unfit for human consumption or noxious. He further submitted that looking to the period of custody already undergone by the revisionist, the matter is not being pleaded on its merit but the only submission is that the same be considered on the ground of sentence since out of the period of one year of imprisonment, fine and default clause, the revisionist has undergone about eight months and eighteen days. 8. The Apex Court in the case of Nand Lal Vs. State of Uttrakhand: (2010) 4 SCC 562 has held that the valid ground for reduction of the sentence is the delay in proceedings and the age of the accused.
